Task 3 is about developing the conceptual design of the conformal tank, as a feasibility study for the final tank to be developed at the end of the program. This was scheduled early in the program to establish feasibility and identify any big risks and/or show-stoppers. Task 4 involves design of the Phase 1 tank test article- a simpler geometry, all composite cryogenic tank with an inner and outer shell. This tank has sufficient design features of the full-scale conformal tank to tackle and eliminate some of the program risks in Phase 1. Task 5 was performed by UDRI and involved materials testing and laminate testing at room temperature and cryogenic temperature. Task 6 involves manufacture of the Phase 1 composite tank, and Task 7 was about boil-off and pressure testing of the tank. These two tasks were not completed. Some planning work for Task 6 was completed. Details are in the next section. Table 1: Tasks description and their completion percentage. Full-scale Phase 2 Tank Conceptual Design A conceptual design of a product-oriented conformable composite tank was completed at the start of the program, providing a target configuration for the development of key enabling technologies during the first phase. Figure 1 shows the concept, consisting of an inner tank capable of holding 0.5 cubic meters of liquid hydrogen with an outer shell. An insulating vacuum space is between the two, with support structures maintaining the gap and transmitting loads from the inner tank to the outer shell.
